Scenario 5 — Protect the healer, keep the finishers fighting
Mage/Warrior/Priest (Team A) versus Mage/Rogue/Priest (Team B)

THE CHALLENGE
Team A trails 17–19; 20 points win. Five ticks remain, from step 295 to 300. Team A needs three kills without conceding a death. Use the terminal Team A reward: +1 SUCCESS, 0 DRAW, −1 FAIL. A simultaneous 20–20 finish is a draw; a winning threshold reached on the final tick still counts as SUCCESS.

The 20 × 10 battlefield has seven pillars. Team A starts with Mage at 15 HP, Warrior at 36 HP and Priest at just 1 HP. Team B starts with Mage at 13 HP, Rogue at 44 HP and Priest at 15 HP. HP means remaining health. Other configured classes start dead and cannot act before the final respawn wave.

THE TEAM PROBLEM
The weakest teammate is the healer—but healing itself is not the plan in this winning example. Warrior protects Priest's approach lanes while Priest spends its turns keeping Warrior and Mage alive. Mage must remove enemy support and then finish Mage-B. These are connected jobs: protection keeps healing available, and healing lets both attackers finish.

THE FEW RULES YOU NEED
Each tick, everyone chooses movement plus Basic, Ultimate or no combat from the same starting state. Ultimate replaces Basic. Damage and healing resolve together. Movement cannot dodge an accepted attack; new stun restricts later decisions. A cooldown counts decisions until an ability is ready.

Mage's Burst spends this tick preparing stronger future Basics. Priest can Basic-heal within distance 3; its powerful Ultimate reaches 5.75, so a teammate can move beyond Basic healing range while remaining reachable by Ultimate. These are center-to-center ranges; the acting agent's exact legal-action mask is always authoritative. Warrior's Charge damages, repositions and applies control. Rogue's Poison damages and causes stun, slow and reduced healing. Priest's Basic heal also briefly protects movement speed from slows; its Ultimate does not apply that speed floor.

Agents are physical discs of radius 0.5. A Warrior body can obstruct Rogue's movement, but it does not block sight or automatically prevent an attack. Collision resolution may move a unit even when it chooses Stay. Nearby Mage and Warrior auras modify damage separately from this physical screen; the HP results below include those effects.

THE OPPONENT
Use SharedObs and Reactive TDM BETA for Team B. SharedObs shares authorized current teammate sightings, not future actions. Rogue pursues an observed living enemy Priest first, Mage second, Hunter third, and attempts glancing shoulder routes past other bodies. Its attacks are chosen independently: the lowest-health legal enemy within Basic radius, Ultimate before Basic. It can therefore attack Warrior while hunting Priest. Other classes follow ALPHA. The same opponent rules run every tick; they are not a prerecorded response sequence.

ONE VERIFIED WINNING SEQUENCE
Directions are movement intentions; collisions determine the final positions. All actions in a row are committed together. Initially dead Team A slots remain Stay/no-combat.

Tick | Mage-A | Warrior-A | Priest-A
1 | Northeast; Burst | North; Charge Rogue-B | South; Basic-heal Warrior-A
2 | Northwest; Basic Priest-B | Stay; Basic Rogue-B | Southeast; Basic-heal Mage-A
3 | West; Basic Priest-B | Stay; Basic Rogue-B | South; Ultimate-heal Mage-A
4 | West; Basic Mage-B | Stay; no combat while stunned | South; Basic-heal Warrior-A
5 | West; Basic Mage-B | East; Basic Rogue-B | Stay; Basic-heal Warrior-A

WHY THE CHOICES WORK TOGETHER
Tick 1: Warrior spends Charge on the pursuer rather than either tempting spellcaster, constraining Rogue's next decision and pressing it toward the northern boundary. Priest moves South into the developing screen and heals Warrior instead of itself. Mage prepares Burst and moves into position for Priest's next Basic heal. Mage-B also chooses Burst here; Mage-A takes no damage on this opening tick.

Tick 2: Mage attacks Priest-B, whose future healing is the threat to this finishing sequence, and moves Northwest while Priest supplies the Basic heal. Mage survives at about 0.58 HP. Priest moves Southeast behind the screen, while Warrior stays and damages the stunned Rogue. The next rescue will use Ultimate's longer reach rather than require continued Basic-range contact.

Tick 3: Mage continues West and finishes Priest-B while Priest's now-ready Ultimate restores Mage to 80 HP. This aggressive move is supported by a heal chosen from the same starting snapshot, not a later reaction. Priest-B began with cooldown 3 and would first have Ultimate on tick 4; it dies before that decision. Meanwhile Warrior Stays and attacks Rogue. Rogue uses Poison on Warrior, not the Priest it is pursuing. Stay is a movement command; body contact can still move Warrior.

Ticks 4–5: Priest returns its healing to Warrior, whose Poison status reduces the healing received. Warrior is stunned on tick 4, then finishes Rogue on tick 5. Mage spends both Basics finishing Mage-B. Priest moves South, then Stays, while Warrior moves East on the final turn. The useful positioning idea is to keep the defender between pursuer and protected teammate, anticipating the likely approach while preserving attacks and healing access. Center-line alignment is a guide, not a guaranteed block or universally best move.

WHAT THIS SCENARIO IS DESIGNED TO TEST
- Teammate Modeling: position for the heal or physical protection a partner can supply next.
- Opponent Modeling: anticipate the Priest-hunting Rogue and enemy healing/Burst timings.
- Tactical Positioning: coordinate the moving screen, healing access and offensive approach.
- Basic Damage Target Prioritization: Mage works through Priest-B before Mage-B while Warrior handles Rogue.
- Basic Healing Target Prioritization: Priest heals Warrior, Mage, then Warrior twice despite its own 1 HP.
- Ultimate Damage Target Prioritization: spend Charge on the immediate pursuer.
- Ultimate Healing Target Prioritization: rescue the 0.58-HP Mage with the longer-range heal.
- Ultimate Timing (Burst): invest tick 1 in stronger attacks for the short finishing window.
- Crowd-Control Prioritization: deny Rogue its tick-2 action instead of controlling another attractive target.

Multi-Step Team-Level Planning: combine the moving body screen, changing healing recipients and Burst-supported damage across all five ticks. This describes the coordinated sequence, not proof that a policy contains an explicit planner.

RESULT AND LIMITS
The corrected route was verified on 2026-09-15 with BETA v4. Scores progress 17–19, 17–19, 18–19, 18–19, then 20–19. Team A wins at step 300 with Mage about 35.15 HP, Warrior about 1 HP and Priest 1 HP. No Team A agent dies. Both termination and truncation flags are true; the reward is still +1. The final wave revives previously dead units, including Priest-B; that does not erase its earlier death or Team A's points.

This is one successful route, not proof that others fail or that a policy reasons this way. Compare methods with matched ablations under a fixed setup and opponent. This is not an Elo score or suite release. Official evaluation material must not guide training or selection.
